newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union sets ultimatum over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German union sets ultimatum over sick pay.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall Thursday began top-level talks with employers hinting at compromise on a bitter dispute over sick pay but threatening industrial action if no deal is reached.

Klaus Zwickel, head of the powerful IG Metall engineering union, said the two sides must find common ground over a new law allowing sick pay to be cut to 80 percent of normal wages from 100 percent currently.
If not, Germany would face a further day of walkouts and protests in the key enginering sector on Oct. 24.
"We are sticking with (our demand for) 100 percent sick pay," Zwickel said as he arrived at a Frankfurt hotel for talks with the engineering employers' association Gesamtmetall.
Gesamtmetall President Werner Stumpfe reaffirmed his commitment to a law aimed at cutting sick pay allowances to 80 percent.
"I couldn't imagine the unions could offer so much that we would move away from this point," Stumpfe told journalists,
The sick-pay cut was backed up by legislation, he said, and as a result should be implemented.

Earlier this week, Gesamtmetall was humiliatingly forced to climb down from its initial firm position on the sick pay issue after walkouts at some of Germany's largest companies disrupted production and caused losses worth millions of dollars.
